metadata.note: The Washington, Baltimore and Annapolis Electric Railway (WB&A, electric 1908-1935) and its steam predecessors on the Annapolis Junction - Annapolis line, the Annapolis and Elk Ridge (1840-1886) and the Annapolis, Washington and Baltimore (1886-1907). WB&A features: the Main Line Baltimore - Washington with its city approaches, the Baltimore terminals (Liberty St 1908-1921, Howard & Lombard 1921-1935), the Washington downtown extension (1910-1935) and its first downtown terminal at 14th St (1910-1921), the South Shore Line Naval Academy Junction - Annapolis, the Annapolis street extension (1913-1923 confirmed), the Camp Meade line west end (1913-1915 and 1921-1923, both open), the 1917 Naval Academy Jct - Admiral anchor, and the Bowie race-track specials (1914-1928, open end). The WB&A's North Shore Line (1921-1935) is drawn in baltimore_and_annapolis_railroad.geojson (feature wba-north-shore-line), whose company string and colour these features reuse. Research report: research/branches/washington_baltimore_and_annapolis_electric_railroad.txt.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), 2026-10-25: rail tiles; ways with old_railway_operator matching 'Washington,? Baltimore|WB&A' and historic:operator 'Washington, Baltimore...' in bbox 38.85,-77.02,39.32,-76.45; abandoned/historic ways and named trails for six gap boxes (Washington, Main Line south and north, South Shore, west end, Baltimore); the abandoned Capital Transit way 169999449; named city streets in Washington (Kenilworth Ave, Benning Rd, H St, Massachusetts Ave, New York Ave), Baltimore (Bush, Scott, McHenry, Portland, Greene, Pratt, Howard, Lombard, Liberty Sts, Hopkins Pl) and Annapolis (West St, Bladen St, College Ave, King George St, Maryland Ave).

OpenHistoricalMap via Overpass, 2026-10-25: 'Washington, Baltimore and Annapolis Electric Railway' ways (start 1908, end 1935) District Line - Linthicum, and the South Shore ways Annapolis Junction - Annapolis carrying dated operator keys for the Annapolis & Elkridge, the AW&B and the WB&A.
metadata.overlap_with_other_layers: Linthicum - Baltimore (Howard & Lombard) on wba-main-line and wba-baltimore-howard-lombard also carried the WB&A North Shore cars 1921-1935; baltimore_and_annapolis_railroad.geojson's wba-north-shore-line deliberately stops at Linthicum so the corridor is drawn once. The two steam features share one geometry (Rule 4 split at the 1886 change of company), which is also the union of wba-south-shore-west-end and wba-south-shore-line. The Light RailLink (no layer yet) reuses the Main Line right-of-way Baltimore Highlands - North Linthicum; if drawn it is a separate Maryland Transit Administration feature.
metadata.ownership_split: Split 1886 (Annapolis and Elk Ridge -> Annapolis, Washington and Baltimore: sold 10 Nov 1885, rechartered 24 Mar 1886) and 1907/08 (AW&B steam trains -> WB&A electric cars, 7 Feb 1908). Not split: the 1903 WB&A purchase of the AW&B (the AW&B kept running its own trains under its own name - Evening Capital 2 Oct 1905), the 1899-1902 WB&A renamings (Potomac and Severn -> Washington and Annapolis -> WB&A; no trains yet), and the January 1931 receivership (the receivers ran the same company's trains). The 1921 Short Line purchase is split in the B&A layer.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn (Rule 1): the South Shore after 20 Aug 1935 (Annapolis Junction - Fort Meade to the B&O and Fort Meade - Academy Junction to the PRR, Fort Meade freight to Dec 1982; Academy Jct - Nevamar spur to 2004); the Camp Meade post tracks (no passenger evidence); Naval Academy Junction shops and yard; the Westport / Scott Street substation and yard; AW&B/WB&A steam freight on the west end after 1908; the Bowie spur's post-1936 PRR operation.
metadata.horsecar: None - the A&ER was steam from 26 Dec 1840, the WB&A electric from 1908, and the Washington and Baltimore street trackage was electric by 1908. Nothing trimmed (Rule 5).
metadata.excluded: Not drawn: report block [7], the wartime Camp Meade post tracks (drawable NONE - no confirmable passenger year); block [9], the North Shore Line (already drawn in baltimore_and_annapolis_railroad.geojson); block [12], Baltimore and Potomac (PRR) trains to Annapolis via Odenton (drawable NONE - no confirmed year, another company); block [13], B&O Fort Meade service after 1935 (drawable NONE - another company, no confirmed year); the post-1935 Fort Meade - Naval Academy Junction and Washington - Annapolis buses (not rail).
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS: wba-south-shore-west-end 1913-1915 (both ends open: 1908-1912 and 1916-1917 not established/checked) and 1921-1923 (rail end somewhere 1923-1935; Evening Capital WB&A ads 1924-1935 would settle it); wba-bowie-race-track-spur 1914-1928 (1929-1935 not checked); wba-annapolis-street-extension 1913-1923 (first and last confirmed years only).
ANCHOR: wba-camp-meade-admiral-1917 - one confirmed year (Evening Star 8 Oct 1917); the exact wartime gap on the west end (when in 1917/18 the tracks went to the government) is not established.
The Baltimore opening day: 19 Mar 1908 (Wikipedia, citing the Baltimore Sun) vs 3 Apr 1908 (Don's Depot).
The AW&B's last steam passenger day, between 14 Oct 1907 and 7 Feb 1908.
The A&ER years (1840-1886) rest on Wikipedia only; not primary-checked.

Washington street routes and track owners 1908-1935 (Fowler queries H St / Massachusetts / New York Aves); Fowler's mileposts District Line 33.6 - White House 36 - New York Ave & 12th 37.7 are shorter than the straight-line distances between those points (3.9 and 2.4 mi), so they cannot be route miles - conflict recorded in geometry_quality.

Baltimore street route Westport - Bush St - Scott / McHenry / Portland / Greene / Pratt Sts and the Liberty St / Lombard St terminal approach (Fowler queries them); whether the street rails were United Railways track; whether Main Line cars left Liberty St entirely in 1921.
The Annapolis street route West St - State House - Naval Academy Gate, and which Academy gate.
Whether the OSM Bowie race-track spur is the WB&A's 1914 spur or the PRR's post-1936 layout.

headway_min everywhere is an estimate except the west end's 1921 'four round trips daily', the AW&B's four weekday trains each way and the Bowie specials' 15 minutes on race days; Main Line frequency conflict (1913/1915 ads roughly hourly vs Wikipedia's half-hourly expresses) recorded.

properties.geometry_quality: Drawn 37.83 mi, Baltimore (Pratt & Howard Sts) - Washington (15th & H Sts NE, 'White House' station). Approximated (straight-line) legs, 2.26 mi in all: Westport grade end - Scott Street south end, 1.72 mi (the Westport tunnel and the private right-of-way past Bush Street are not mapped in OSM or OHM; the straight line passes within ~25 m of Bush Street's south-east end); two gaps between the OSM WB&A grade fragments at Lansdowne/Westport, 0.43 mi together; Capital Transit grade west end - Kenilworth Ave at Deanwood, 0.11 mi. Traced breakdown: Baltimore streets 1.09 mi (Scott St, McHenry/Portland St, Greene St, Pratt St - the streets Fowler names, which he himself queries, so the city routing is a plausible placement, not a sourced one; whether the rails were United Railways track is not established); Westport grade end - District Line 30.44 mi, of which 29.1 mi on WB&A-own ways (OHM WB&A ways, the WB&A Trail and other OSM WB&A-tagged grade, WB&A-tagged Light RailLink track), 0.5 mi near Linthicum on an OHM way named for the Short Line that coincides within ~25 m with OSM's WB&A-tagged path there, 0.1 mi of short connectors; District Line - Deanwood 1.81 mi on the abandoned Capital Transit (ex-Washington Railway & Electric Seat Pleasant line) grade; Deanwood - 15th & H NE 2.62 mi on Kenilworth Ave NE and Benning Road. DOCUMENTED MILEAGE (FOWLER-INT table 208 mileposts): Baltimore Terminal 0.0, Westport 2.9, Naval Academy Junction 15.6, District Line 33.6, Washington White House 36. Drawn: Pratt & Howard - District Line 33.25 mi (+0.42 mi on to the Liberty St terminal = 33.67 vs 33.6, ~0%); Westport grade end - District Line 30.44 vs 30.7 (-1%); Pratt & Howard - Naval Academy Jct 15.23 (+0.42 = 15.65 vs 15.6). District Line - 15th & H NE is drawn 4.58 mi against Fowler's 2.4: Fowler's figure cannot be route miles, because the straight-line distance between the two points is 3.9 mi, so the conflict is recorded rather than resolved (the research report's own estimate is 'roughly 3-4 mi'). FIT: OHM draws the WB&A coarsely (vertices up to 3.4 km apart near Severn Run), but every vertex of OSM's WB&A-tagged grade along the main line lies within 27 m of the drawn line. LATER ALIGNMENTS: Baltimore Highlands - North Linthicum is drawn on the Light RailLink track rebuilt on the WB&A right-of-way in 1992-93 (OSM tags it historic:operator WB&A), so local curvature there is the 1990s rebuild's; Glenn Dale - Bowie - Bragers follows the WB&A Trail rail-trail; the DC and Baltimore street legs follow today's street geometry (Kenilworth Ave is now a freeway with a surface road, drawn on the surface road; the Benning Road bridge has been rebuilt). The 1908-1921 Baltimore terminal (Liberty St) and 1921-1935 terminal (Howard & Lombard) are separate features continuing from this feature's Pratt & Howard end.

segments.note: WB&A Main Line Baltimore - Washington, with its city approaches: Westport - Bush St - city streets to Pratt & Howard in Baltimore (report block [4]) and District Line - Deanwood - Kenilworth Ave - Benning Road - 15th & H Sts NE ('White House' station) in Washington (block [2], which stayed in use after the 1910 downtown extension: Bowie race specials left from it in 1914-1928). Opened with an invited trip Baltimore - Academy Junction - Annapolis - Washington on 7 Feb 1908 (Washington Herald 8 Feb 1908); public Baltimore service 19 Mar 1908 (Wikipedia, citing the Baltimore Sun) or 3 Apr 1908 (Don's Depot) - CONFLICT recorded, year agreed. 6,600 V 25 Hz AC from 1908, 1,200 V DC from 1910; until the DC cars of 15 Feb 1910 passengers transferred to local cars at 15th & H NE (Herald 1908; Don's Depot). Receivership from January 1931 (same company, same trains). From 1921 the North Shore cars from Annapolis also ran Linthicum - Baltimore over this line (the B&A layer's wba-north-shore-line stops at Linthicum so as not to draw it twice). Last train left the Washington terminal at 12:04 a.m. on 21 Aug 1935 (Evening Star 21 Aug 1935). headway_min 60 is an ESTIMATE from the 1913 and 1915 Evening Capital ads, which give Washington departures roughly hourly with extras; Wikipedia (from Harwood) speaks of half-hourly expresses in the 1910s-20s - conflict recorded, the hourly figure used. Up to 84 special trains a day ran for Camp Meade in 1918 (Wikipedia).
sources: Segment-level: start 1908 from the Washington Herald 8 Feb 1908 p.12 (opening trip), end 1935 from the Evening Star 21 Aug 1935 p.2 (last train), service frequency from the Evening Capital ads of 14 Nov 1913 and 27 Oct 1915, as read in research/branches/washington_baltimore_and_annapolis_electric_railroad.txt block [1]; Baltimore opening day secondary (Wikipedia vs Don's Depot, in conflict); headway an estimate.

segments.note: Naval Academy Junction - Odenton - Admiral - Portland - Disney - Annapolis Junction. Drawn 1913-1915 from two dated ads whose footnotes have trains that 'connect at Odenton with P.R.R.' and at 'Annapolis Junction with B.&O.R.R.' (Evening Capital 14 Nov 1913 and 27 Oct 1915) - the OCR loses which trains and how many. BOTH ENDS ARE OPEN: 1913 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start (1908-1912 not established; the line had trolley wire by July 1909, which is not passenger evidence), and 1915 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end (1916-1917 not checked). The through service was then withdrawn for the war, the tracks 'turned over to the government' (Evening Star 3 Jun 1921) - so the 1915-1921 gap is deliberate. Do not close it or extend without evidence. headway_min 240 is an ESTIMATE (the 1921 restoration ran four round trips daily).
sources: Segment-level: connection footnotes in the Evening Capital ads of 14 Nov 1913 p.3 and 27 Oct 1915 p.3, as read in the research report block [6]; which trains ran through, and how often, not established. Headway an estimate.

segments.note: Camp Meade line restored: 'would begin service Monday [6 Jun 1921] between Naval Academy Junction and Camp Meade Junction, the connecting point with the Baltimore and Ohio railroad. The service will begin with four round trips daily ... This was the service that was discontinued during the war' (Evening Star 3 Jun 1921). 'Camp Meade' still in the WB&A service heading in May 1923 (Evening Capital 9 May 1923: 'Washington and Camp Meade passengers change at Naval Academy Junction'). 1923 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end: rail service ended at some unknown date before Aug 1935, by when a bus ran Fort Meade - Naval Academy Junction (Evening Star 21 Aug 1935) - the bus is not rail evidence. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 240 from the 1921 'four round trips daily'.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Evening Star 3 Jun 1921 p.13 (restoration, four round trips), 1923 from the Evening Capital 9 May 1923 p.2, as read in the research report block [6]; end open.

SEASONAL - a few weeks each spring and autumn; the map cannot show seasonality. 1928 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end: 1929-1935 were not checked, and buses competed from 1926. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 15 is the race-day figure of the 1926/1928 notices, on race days only.

segments.note: Steam from opening: construction finished 25 Dec 1840 and service inaugurated 26 Dec 1840 at 6 a.m. from West Street (Wikipedia, citing Harwood); connections with the B&O at Annapolis Junction for Baltimore and Washington (fares 1840: $2 to Baltimore, $2.50 to Washington). No horse era - nothing trimmed under Rule 5. Short interruptions: May-July 1841 (engine-house fire, 18 May 1841) and 21 Apr 1861 (track torn up, repaired by Butler's troops). Sold 10 Nov 1885 and rechartered as the Annapolis, Washington and Baltimore on 24 Mar 1886, which ran the trains from then (separate feature). headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE; no A&ER timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: secondary only - dates from Wikipedia (Annapolis and Elk Ridge Railroad, citing Harwood and an archived mdoe.org page), not primary-checked; the 1885/86 transfer NOT SOURCED beyond Wikipedia. Headway an estimate.

segments.note: Steam trains of the Annapolis, Washington and Baltimore Railroad, rechartered 24 Mar 1886 out of the A&ER (Wikipedia). The WB&A bought the company in 1903, but the AW&B kept running its own trains under its own name - 'Annapolis, Washington & Balto. R.R. Time Schedule', columns 'VIA A.W.&B. AND P.R.R.' and 'VIA A.W.&B. AND B.&O.R.R.', four weekday trains each way (Evening Capital 2 Oct 1905) - so 1903 is a control change, not a split. Still advertising its own trains on 14 Oct 1907 (schedule of 9 Jun 1907, connecting with the Pennsylvania at Odenton and the B&O at Annapolis Junction); steam passenger service ended between mid-Oct 1907 and the WB&A electric opening of 7 Feb 1908, the last day NOT ESTABLISHED. Freight on the west end continued by steam after 1908 (not drawn). headway_min 240 is derived from the four weekday trains each way of the 1905-1907 schedules.
sources: Segment-level: AW&B timetables in the Evening Capital 2 Oct 1905, 14 Dec 1906, 31 May 1907 and 14 Oct 1907 (all p.3), as read in the research report block [11]; the 1886 recharter from Wikipedia only.
